chunks.title: PulseGrid — Real-Time IoT Monitoring Dashboard
chunks.text:
PulseGrid — Real-Time IoT Monitoring Dashboard (IoT · Full Stack · Real-time), a featured project.
Live IoT monitoring platform: simulated sensor devices stream over MQTT to a FastAPI backend and a real-time React dashboard, with InfluxDB Cloud history. (Aug 2026)
Impact: Real-time IoT monitoring platform: devices → MQTT (HiveMQ Cloud) → FastAPI → WebSocket → React, with InfluxDB Cloud history; deployed on Vercel and Render.
Tech stack: React.js, TypeScript, FastAPI (Python), MQTT (HiveMQ Cloud), InfluxDB Cloud, WebSocket, Apache ECharts, Vercel, Render.
Live demo: https://pulsegrid-xi.vercel.app/
Case study: /projects/pulsegrid

chunks.title: PulseGrid — Real-Time IoT Monitoring Dashboard — Problem
chunks.text: Monitoring building metrics (lighting, water, carbon intensity, energy and footfall) means moving device telemetry to a dashboard in real time, keeping its history for analysis, and sending commands back to the devices, across separately hosted services.

chunks.title: PulseGrid — Real-Time IoT Monitoring Dashboard — Solution
chunks.text:
A full-stack real-time pipeline: simulated sensor devices publish over **MQTT** (HiveMQ Cloud, TLS/MQTT5), a **FastAPI** backend consumes the stream and pushes it over **WebSocket** to a live **React** dashboard, and **InfluxDB Cloud** stores the time-series history.

It runs as a split-stack production deployment: the React/Vite frontend on **Vercel**, the FastAPI backend on **Render** with an in-process background simulator task, environment-based configuration, and scoped MQTT credentials/ACL permissions.

chunks.title: PulseGrid — Real-Time IoT Monitoring Dashboard — Result
chunks.text: A stable, always-on data pipeline, live at [pulsegrid-xi.vercel.app](https://pulsegrid-xi.vercel.app/) (built Aug 2026), with time-series history for lighting, water, carbon intensity, energy and footfall metrics.

chunks.title: PulseGrid — Real-Time IoT Monitoring Dashboard — Features
chunks.text:
- Live dashboard fed over WebSocket from the MQTT stream
- Time-series history in InfluxDB Cloud across five metric families
- **Analyse** view with live side-by-side metric comparison
- **Control** panel that sends real-time device commands back over MQTT
- Charts built with Apache ECharts

chunks.title: PulseGrid — Real-Time IoT Monitoring Dashboard — Challenges
chunks.text:
Several live production issues had to be diagnosed and fixed end-to-end before the pipeline was stable and always-on:

- **MQTT protocol and session handling** between the backend and the broker
- **Broker credential permissions** (scoped credentials and ACLs)
- A **topic-namespace mismatch** between publisher and subscriber

chunks.title: PulseGrid — Real-Time IoT Monitoring Dashboard — Architecture
chunks.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  devices["Simulated sensor devices"] -->|"MQTT (TLS / MQTT5)"| broker["HiveMQ Cloud"]
  broker --> api["FastAPI backend on Render"]
  api -->|time-series| influx[("InfluxDB Cloud")]
  api -->|WebSocket| ui["React dashboard on Vercel"]
  ui -->|"device commands"| api
  api -->|MQTT| broker
```

chunks.title: Human Resource Management System (HRMS) — Problem
chunks.text: A funded SaaS startup needed an HRMS for a live, multi-tenant customer base: payroll, attendance, leave and analytics, with each organization's data kept strictly separate, and HR reporting that had been done manually.

chunks.title: Human Resource Management System (HRMS) — Solution
chunks.text:
35+ HRMS modules built with **React.js**, **NestJS/Node.js** and **PostgreSQL**, with clean, well-organized service/controller code.

- **Multi-tenant isolation:** an organization ID on every record, Prisma middleware and JWT-based checks, with role-based access enforced on every API endpoint
- **Secure APIs** with JWT and role-based access, documented with Swagger
- **Production hosting** on a self-managed Ubuntu 24.04 server: Nginx reverse proxy, PM2 process management and Let's Encrypt SSL/HTTPS for both the app and the API
- **Git-based deployments** with Prisma migrations

chunks.title: Human Resource Management System (HRMS) — Result
chunks.text: The HRMS is live at [orglineai.com](https://orglineai.com), serving 500+ users across 35+ modules. Filter-based dashboards replaced manual HR reporting, and automated backups plus PM2 keep the app recovering cleanly after crashes or reboots.

chunks.title: Human Resource Management System (HRMS) — Features
chunks.text:
- Payroll, attendance, leave and analytics modules (35+ in total)
- Live, filterable HR dashboards in place of manual reports
- Role-based access on every API endpoint
- Full Swagger API documentation
- Responsive, production-ready UI built from Figma designs

chunks.title: Human Resource Management System (HRMS) — Challenges
chunks.text:
- **Slow endpoints on large record sets:** rebuilt with server-side pagination and targeted PostgreSQL indexes
- **Running production safely on a self-managed server:** hardened with a UFW firewall, fail2ban and a dedicated non-root deploy user, with automated PostgreSQL backups before every deploy
- **Tenant data isolation:** enforced in the data layer (organization ID + Prisma middleware) and again at the API (JWT checks), not only in the UI

chunks.title: Human Resource Management System (HRMS) — Architecture
chunks.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  browser["React.js app"] -->|HTTPS| nginx["Nginx reverse proxy + Let's Encrypt"]
  nginx --> api["NestJS API (PM2)"]
  api -->|"Prisma (org ID on every record)"| db[("PostgreSQL")]
  db -.->|"backup before every deploy"| backups["Automated backups"]
  subgraph vps["Ubuntu 24.04 VPS (UFW, fail2ban)"]
    nginx
    api
    db
  end
```

chunks.title: WaNotifier — Real-Time IoT Alert System
chunks.text:
WaNotifier — Real-Time IoT Alert System (IoT · Cloud · Serverless), a featured project.
Device events to WhatsApp alerts in under 2 seconds: MQTT → AWS IoT Core → API Gateway → Lambda, fully serverless. (May 2024)
Impact: Device → MQTT → AWS IoT Core → API Gateway/Lambda → WhatsApp alerts in under 2 seconds; X.509 device certificates and policy-based access.
Tech stack: AWS IoT Core, MQTT, AWS API Gateway, AWS Lambda, Python, Node.js.
Case study: /projects/wanotifier

chunks.title: WaNotifier — Real-Time IoT Alert System — Problem
chunks.text: Device events need to reach people quickly, as a WhatsApp notification, without running servers, and the devices themselves must be authenticated before they can publish.

chunks.title: WaNotifier — Real-Time IoT Alert System — Solution
chunks.text:
A full IoT flow built at SAS Automation: device telemetry is published over **MQTT** to **AWS IoT Core**, routed through **AWS API Gateway** and **Lambda**, and delivered as a **WhatsApp** alert.

The backend is an event-driven, serverless setup on AWS with auto-scaling, and devices are secured with AWS IoT Core **X.509 certificates** and policy-based access.

chunks.title: WaNotifier — Real-Time IoT Alert System — Result
chunks.text: Under 2 seconds from device event to WhatsApp notification, on serverless infrastructure that scales automatically.

chunks.title: WaNotifier — Real-Time IoT Alert System — Features
chunks.text:
- End-to-end device → cloud → WhatsApp alert pipeline
- Event-driven, auto-scaling serverless backend
- Device authentication with X.509 certificates
- Policy-based access control in AWS IoT Core

chunks.title: WaNotifier — Real-Time IoT Alert System — Architecture
chunks.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  device["IoT device"] -->|"MQTT (X.509)"| iot["AWS IoT Core"]
  iot --> gw["AWS API Gateway"]
  gw --> lambda["AWS Lambda"]
  lambda --> wa["WhatsApp alert"]
```

chunks.title: E-Commerce Platform — Problem
chunks.text: An online store needs a fast storefront for customers and a separate, protected place for staff to manage inventory and orders, with invoices and failures handled cleanly.

chunks.title: E-Commerce Platform — Solution
chunks.text:
Built at SAS Automation as a full-stack store on **React.js**, **Node.js/Express.js** and **MySQL**.

- Reusable React.js components (multi-step forms, validation, data tables) for the storefront and the admin panel
- REST APIs for product listings, order management and secure PDF invoice generation, with error-handling middleware so failures surface clearly instead of failing silently
- Secure **JWT** login with protected routes and a **Redux** global cart

chunks.title: E-Commerce Platform — Result
